newsitem.title: FRANCE: French company tax rise a certainty - Le Monde.
newsitem.headline: French company tax rise a certainty - Le Monde.

text.p: The French government has decided to increase company taxes but is still studying other options for curbing the budget deficit, afternoon daily Le Monde said.

It said the government planned a package of measures worth around 30 billion francs to reduce the budget deficit to around 3.3 percent of gross domestic product from 3.6 to 3.7, the figure expected from an audit of public finances due on Monday.
"An increase in taxes on companies is a certainty," it said.

The government would leave the basic rate of tax unchanged at 33.3 percent but increase a 10 percent surcharge on this introduced in 1995. This would bring the effective tax rate to nearly 40 percent from the current 36.6, it said. The increase would be for 1997 and 1998.

It said the government was studying an increase in employer contributions to the pensions system, accompanied by measures to protect the low paid from being affected by this. No decision had yet been taken.
The government had decided against increasing wealth taxes or savings taxes in 1997, ideas it initially considered.
It was considering cancelling income tax cuts due this year, though this would affect only those on high incomes.
